analyst_view.overall: Early view: Amed (3rd) have one of the league's most productive attacks (28 goals) and beat Eyupspor 5-1 in their last home game before the trip to Galatasaray. Alanyaspor (13th) under Joao Pereira had lost four straight by the break and have scored nine all season. Both have two more league games first, including Amed's trip to Gaziantep, so form and team news can shift.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.7 goals and I lean slightly lower. Amed should score two or three at home, but Alanyaspor's expected 1.0 looks high for a side with one goal in their last three games, so I see about three in total.

corners.text: The numbers say 8.0 corners and I lean higher. Amed won six corners even at Galatasaray and are a set-piece threat, so at home against a side that has spent recent games pinned back they should push the count up.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.6 cards. Amed have collected cards recently (three at Galatasaray and Ballet's red-card ban), but nothing is reported about Alanyaspor's discipline, so I stay near the number.

shots.text: The numbers say 27.0 shots, 17.6 of them Amed's. Hasi's side took 14 shots even at Galatasaray, so a high home total is realistic, and Alanyaspor's 9.4 is already modest.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.1 shots on target. Amed's forwards Gift Orban and Mbaye Diagne get on the end of plenty of chances, but Alanyaspor will add little, so I keep it close to nine.
